kept.title: A 10-unit EIP-3009 authorization over someone else's top-up nonce closes their quote; the buyer's real payment is never credited
kept.mechanism: topup._terms() deliberately accepts any positive payment (`amount_units=1`) so that underpayments are credited. EIP-3009 nonces are per signer, so anyone can sign their own authorization over a quote's nonce. settle.verify_transfer binds the FIRST matching authorization whose next transfer is >= seller_units (`if ... or bound_pays: continue` at settle.py:487, `bound_pays = moved[2] >= terms.seller_units` at settle.py:513). With seller_units=1, a dust authorization satisfies that check. redeem() then credits min(paid, quote), moves the quote to CREDITED permanently, and answers 409 `topup_already_credited` to any other tx (topup.py:572-576). This defeats the 'every match is tried' defence that settle.py was hardened with for the invoke rail.
kept.failure_scenario: 1) A buyer takes a $100 quote (nonce N) and pays 100 USDC with transferWithAuthorization over N. 2) Once that tx is mined, N is public in the AuthorizationUsed log. 3) An attacker signs its own authorization over N for 10 base units to the hub's top-up wallet and sends it; on Base this confirms in a few seconds. 4) The attacker calls the open endpoint POST /topups/N with its own tx before the buyer redeems. The deposit watcher scans only every AIMARKET_DEPOSIT_WATCH_INTERVAL_S (60 s), and the well-known tells buyers that presenting a payment is optional. Result: the quote is CREDITED for 1 millicent ($0.00001). The buyer's 100 USDC redemption gets 409, and the watcher files the buyer's tx as UNATTRIBUTED with 'quote refused', which is never credited automatically. The 100 USDC stays in the operator wallet without credit until the operator reconciles by hand. A same-transaction variant (dust authorization bundled ahead of the buyer's) marks the buyer's own tx CREDITED for $0.00001, so it is not even listed as unattributed. The attacker needs no account, and each attack costs about $0.001 in gas, so it can be repeated against every top-up on a hub.
kept.evidence: topup.py:504-507 `pay_to=q.pay_to, amount_units=1, amount_usd=q.amount_usd(decimals),` (docstring: 'Any positive amount ... is accepted here'); settle.py:487 `if (topics[2] or "").lower() != want_nonce or bound_pays: continue`; settle.py:512-513 `elif moved[1] == want_to: paid, authorizer, bound_pays = moved[2], who, moved[2] >= terms.seller_units`; topup.py:573-575 `if tx_hash and tx_hash != q.tx_hash: raise TopupError(409, "topup_already_credited", ...)`; deposit_watch.py:435-442: rows with QUOTE_REFUSED are 'Never credited automatically'.

kept.title: Credits and channel calls are captured before the answer is built, so an error after capture returns 500 with the buyer charged and the seller paid; a provider can trigger it on purpose
kept.mechanism: _local_deliver runs _local_settle at line 56 first. That captures the hold, and on the credits rail it also pays the publisher share inside the same transaction. It sets local.resolved=True. Only after that do _local_provenance and _local_answer run. (1) _local_provenance line 670 calls `or result.pop("_provenance_receipt", None)` whenever no 'provenance' plugin returned a receipt. When the provider's `result` is a string, list, number or null, this raises AttributeError or TypeError. (2) _local_answer line 723 calls `JSONResponse(status_code=200, content=response_body, ...)`. Starlette serialises with allow_nan=False, so a NaN or Infinity anywhere in the result raises ValueError. httpx parses a provider body containing `NaN` into float('nan') without complaint. Neither case is checked before capture. _local_refuse_undelivered only refuses dicts with ok/success false. Because resolved=True, _local_unwind releases nothing.
kept.failure_scenario: Credits are on. The buyer has a $1.00 key. A listed provider at $0.01 answers {"result": {"temp_c": NaN}}; a Python json.dumps default emits that, and so can a malicious seller. The hub captures $0.01, credits the publisher 70%, then raises ValueError, and the buyer gets HTTP 500 with no output. A client that retries without an Idempotency-Key is charged again on every attempt. A seller who always returns NaN collects 70% of every call and delivers nothing. The same happens with {"result": "text"} or {"result": [..]} on hubs without the provenance plugin (a plain pip install). It also happens on Docker hubs whenever the plugin's receipt issuance fails and it returns None. A deferred Pay-on-Verified channel hold is likewise left for the verdict to capture, over an output the buyer never received.

The capture is at lines 417-420 (`credits_ledger.capture_hold(nonce, publisher_share=share)`) and is followed by `local.resolved = True` at line 438. The provider result comes from line 251, `result = payload.get("result", payload.get("output", payload))`, and can be any JSON type. The installed 3.17.0 artifact (apex) has the same order.

kept.title: Federated sale paid with credits still stores the buyer's escrow authorization, which blocks collection of the whole escrow window; the routing fee is also skipped
kept.mechanism: _fed_escrow_authorization verifies and stores a payment_authorization whenever the channel is escrow-bound (`if crypto_on and not sandbox_mode and x_payment_channel:` ... `if fed.escrow_binding and fed_authorized_total > 0:` -> bridge_auth.verify_and_store). Unlike the local branch, it never checks whether credits pay instead. The local branch has `escrow_pays = not credit_account and not (x402 ok)` (local_admission.py:352), added in 75cb486c2 because 'an authorization stored for it would claim money the ledger never took'. That fix was not carried to the federated branch. _fed_trial_or_hold then takes the credits branch first (`fed_price > 0 and credit_account ...` -> credits_ledger.hold(credit_account, fed_price, fed_nonce)), so no channel hold exists under the buyer's receiptId. _fed_reserve_routing_fee skips the fee because `fed_authorization is not None` ('Already inside the single authorized hold'), but that hold was never taken. On success fed.settled=True, so _fed_unwind (`if fed_authorization is not None and not fed_settled`) never withdraws the stored row.
kept.failure_scenario: Preconditions: crypto on, credits on, and the peer listed in AIMARKET_SELLS_FOR or AIMARKET_PEER_API_KEYS. A buyer sends X-API-Key together with X-Payment-Channel/Secret for an escrow-bound channel and a valid payment_authorization (running total at nonce N). Result: 200; credits are charged the price only, and a resold call skips the routing fee. The authorization row R is stored and supersedes (abandons) the window's previous running-total row. The channel ledger has no debited_receipts row for R, so mirror guard 2 (_ledger_debited_cents(R) is None) reports BLOCKED. Every later channel call at nonce N carries R's units in its running total and is BLOCKED as over-collection. Neither the earlier calls in the window nor the calls until the rows' deadlines lapse can ever be collected on chain. That loss is bounded by AIMARKET_ESCROW_MAX_UNCOLLECTED_USD (default $5) per window. The depositor can then close the escrow and reclaim the full deposit. A buyer can repeat this deliberately for free service, and a client that sends both headers by accident loses the operator that revenue.

kept.title: Bridge losses on undelivered paid calls are never charged to the buyer: one $0.05 top-up lets a buyer and a seller drain the bridge wallet
kept.mechanism: The paid-only gate in reserve() (line 493) compares topped_up_mc with buyer_spent_usd(), and buyer_spent_usd counts only `status IN ('reserved', 'signed', 'delivered')` (line 462). When a paid call ends any other way, finish() / _fed_unwind mark the row 'undelivered', 'unknown' or 'refused', the credit hold is released, and the payment stops counting against the buyer. These cases are: the seller answers 200 with success:false or ok:false (federated_delivery.py:481 `refused = ...`, then 528-541 skip the capture), answers 5xx after it settled, answers 402 again after it settled, sends a non-object or non-JSON body, hits _post_check, or runs past the 30 s safe_post timeout. Each such call moves real USDC to the seller and charges the buyer nothing. Nothing per buyer limits how often this can happen. The only limits are per call ($0.05), per payee per day ($0.50), and AIMARKET_X402_BRIDGE_DAY_USD, which is off by default and not set in the prod roll.
kept.failure_scenario: A seller that is an admitted peer (x402 seller_direct or payment.enforced in its well-known) works with a buyer account that topped up $0.05 once. On every paid call the seller settles the bridge's EIP-3009 authorization and answers 200 {"success": false, ...work...}. The buyer gets HTTP 200 with the body and $0 charged, and the bridge pays $0.05 each time. Repeating this drains the whole bridge wallet, and does so again after every operator top-up, since 'the limit is the wallet balance'. An honest seller can be used for griefing the same way: inputs that make it answer ok:false, run longer than 30 s, or return a JSON array.

kept.title: Replaying a delivered escrow authorization with a wrong channel secret makes the hub abandon its own on-chain claim, so the call goes uncollected
kept.mechanism: verify_and_store treats a resent receipt as a new call: `if live is not None and str(live.receipt_id).lower() == str(auth.receipt_id).lower(): live = None` (l.213-216), so carried_units=0 and every check passes again while the original row X is still PENDING. `authorizations.record(X)` then fails. SQLite reports the newer partial unique index `idx_auth_channel_nonce_active` before the receipt PK ("UNIQUE constraint failed: debit_authorizations.escrow_channel, debit_authorizations.nonce"), so store.record raises the "at nonce ... already stored" message. That sends the call into the supersede branch: `existing = authorizations.active_at(...)` returns X itself, `int(auth.amount) >= int(existing.amount_units)` holds, and `authorizations.abandon(existing.receipt_id, store.SUPERSEDED_REASON)` (l.320) abandons X. The re-record then hits the PK and raises AuthorizationRejected. Nothing revives X. The replay reaches this code because the invoke phases run `_local_escrow_authorization` before `_local_reserve` (local_admission.py:77), and the federated path does the same, so the channel secret is checked only after verify_and_store. The idempotency middleware scopes escrow retries as `owner = "escrow:" + sha256(channel\nsecret)` (idempotency.py:292). Any different secret, or no secret header, is therefore a fresh request that skips the stored answer.
kept.failure_scenario: The buyer owns an escrow-funded ledger channel. (1) It invokes a $0.02 capability with authorization X (receiptId R, nonce N, the first call in the window) and the correct secret. The provider runs, the hold is captured (ledger used 0.02) and X is PENDING for the mirror. (2) It resends the same body with `X-Payment-Channel-Secret: wrong`. Answer: 402 "an authorization for receipt R is already stored", but X is now ABANDONED and `unresolved()` is empty. kept.title: Withdrawing a call that was already superseded is a no-op, so its amount stays in the successor and the whole window becomes uncollectable

Its amount stays inside the successor's signed total, its hold is released, and the ledger never records a debit under its receipt. Mirror guard 2 (`recorded = ledger(row) + Σ ledger(superseded)`) then finds the live row over-collecting and BLOCKS it. kept.title: HORKOS: a signed debit whose broadcast never reached a node leaves a permanent account-nonce gap that stalls every later debit
kept.mechanism: After mark_signed, send_raw failing with RpcUnavailable (every endpoint timing out or returning HTTP 429, or a node rejection whose message lacks 'revert', such as insufficient funds for gas) leaves the row 'signed' at account nonce N. The nonce is never handed out again, by design (mark_dead returns only unsigned nonces). HORKOS stores only raw_keccak, not the raw transaction, so it can never rebroadcast. The hub's retry of the same receipt gets 409 reserved_unresolved until the deadline. Every new debit on any channel is signed at N+1, N+2… and sits in the mempool behind the gap or is rejected. Boot sets `next = max(chain pending count, highest live + 1)`, so a restart keeps the gap while any later row is still live. On the hub those later debits are SUBMITTED with hashes that never mine, and the hub never re-asks for them (see the SUBMITTED dead-end finding), so they stay stuck after HORKOS recovers.
kept.failure_scenario: The public Base RPCs rate-limit HORKOS for a moment, or the hot key runs out of ETH, during one eth_sendRawTransaction. That debit stays 'signed' at nonce N. From then on every debit HORKOS signs for every AICOM hub channel gets a higher nonce and cannot be mined. The hub marks them SUBMITTED ('not mined yet' forever). Escrow collection stops for all channels until an operator notices, waits out the deadlines and restarts, or fills nonce N by hand. Windows whose authorizations expire meanwhile are lost.

kept.title: Idempotency record is dropped on a 403 that follows paid subcontractor work, so a retry with the same key re-runs and re-charges the children
kept.mechanism: InvokeIdempotency.finish deletes the stored answer for any status in NOT_KEPT (401, 403, 404, 405, 413, 415, 422, 429, 503), on the premise that these come 'before any money could move'. A root job with a subcontract allowance violates that premise. Its children capture from the allowance while the root provider runs. The output post-check (_post_check) can then return 403 plugin_blocked_response. invoke_funding.finish keeps the 403 and adds the 'subcontracting' block with spent_from_allowance_usd: the children remain charged and only the root's own hold is refunded.
kept.failure_scenario: A buyer calls POST /invoke with X-API-Key, an Idempotency-Key and `subcontract: {allowance_usd: ...}`. The root provider buys two child calls ($X captured from the allowance), then builtin_safety or a plugin blocks the root output with 403. The idempotency row is deleted. The buyer's client times out and retries with the same key and body, as the README instructs. A fresh job opens, the children run and are charged again, and a deterministic block repeats on every retry. Each retry costs the children's price, although the feature promises 'a retry is not a second purchase'.

kept.mechanism: verifyEquation only checks pi^l * g^r == y (mod N), with l merely odd and in [2,2^128) (_validL). l is not bound to hash_to_prime(g,y,T), and T is chosen by the signer at settlement (it is not committed at closeEntries). So the prover can pick any pi and any small l, then set y = pi^l * g^r mod N. That passes with no sequential work and no root extraction. AIAgentLottery._randomWord (AIAgentLottery.sol:638-649) derives the word from keccak256(canonicalY(y)), so grinding pi picks the winner. The audit's 'forging a chosen y needs an l-th root' argument misses this: the attacker never needs a specific y, only one whose hash lands on the right ticket. DEFAULT_ADMIN can also flip setOnchainVdf (line 810) between closeEntries and fulfillDraw, because the flag is not snapshotted per round.
kept.failure_scenario: A lottery is deployed with onchainVdf=true, as DeployLottery.s.sol:16-17 ('For real value ... set ONCHAIN_VDF=true') and AUDIT.md:72-73 ('prefer onchainVdf=true for value') advise. Three agents buy tickets and the operator commits platonRandom at closeEntries. After the seed block is mined, the ORACLE_SIGNER computes g = hashToGroup(toHex(baseSeed)), takes l=3 and T=1, and tries pi=2,3,... until keccak(y) % totalWeight selects its own or a colluding ticket. It signs the beacon over that proofHash and fulfillDraw accepts it. The signer takes the whole pot every round. With onchainVdf=false it could only abort.
kept.evidence: ChronosVDF.sol:49-53: '// NOTE: this does NOT fully re-derive l == hash_to_prime(g,y,T) on-chain ... if (!_validL(l)) return false;'. AIAgentLottery.sol:639-649: 'require(ChronosVDF.verifyEquation(vdf.N, vdf.g, vdf.y, vdf.pi, vdf.l, vdf.T), "vdf"); ... require(vdf.T == vdfT, "T"); ... return uint256(keccak256(ChronosVDF.canonicalY(vdf.y, vdf.N)));'. DeployLottery.s.sol:16-17: 'For real value, set ... ONCHAIN_VDF=true'.
kept.prod_reachability: Not reachable today. ONCHAIN_VDF is 'false' in docker-compose.yml and docker-compose.uni.yml and onchainVdf=false on Base 0xEcB3A01b44 (per the onchain journal), and paid tickets are off. It becomes reachable as soon as someone follows the documented real-value recipe, or if DEFAULT_ADMIN calls setOnchainVdf(true) mid-round. On Base all roles are the same address 0x1218…Ad0a.
kept.suggested_fix: Do not derive the word from prover-chosen y unless l is Fiat-Shamir-bound on-chain. Either keep onchainVdf off and remove the 'prefer onchainVdf=true for value' advice, or commit T (and ideally N and the l derivation) at closeEntries and bind l = H(g,y,T) on-chain. Snapshot onchainVdf per round at openRound.

kept.title: EVM lottery: an Open round has no permissionless exit, so tickets and sponsor funding are locked if the operator stops
kept.mechanism: Only OPERATOR_ROLE can move a round out of Open: closeEntries (line 438) and cancelRound (line 722). cancelStalledRound (743-749) is permissionless but accepts only Status.Drawing. refund (753-755) requires Cancelled. fund() is permissionless. The Solana port fixed exactly this gap: OPEN_ABANDON_GRACE_SECS and cancel_expired_round (solana lib.rs:50, 415-436), commit f9c72ead3 ('Refunds from a stuck lottery round depended on the authority key staying alive'). The EVM contract was not given the same fix. The header claims 'funds are never held hostage', and AUDIT.md L16 claims a pause cannot trap entries.
kept.failure_scenario: An operator opens a round. Players buy tickets and/or a benefactor or Hub tithe calls fund(). The operator key is then lost, or the operator simply stops running the relayer; the admin may also pause, as was done on Base. Ten years later cancelStalledRound reverts WrongStatus, closeEntries reverts AccessControl, and refund reverts WrongStatus. All ticket ETH and sponsor funding stay in the contract with no exit.

kept.title: A dust EIP-3009 authorization over someone else's top-up nonce closes their quote and strands their real payment
kept.mechanism: Redemption accepts any authorization over the quote nonce that moves at least 1 base unit to pay_to (_terms: `amount_units=1`). The first redemption presented moves the quote to CREDITED, and every other transaction for that nonce is then refused (`if q.status == CREDITED: if tx_hash and tx_hash != q.tx_hash: raise TopupError(409, "topup_already_credited", ...)`). EIP-3009 nonces are per authorizer, so anyone can sign over the same nonce. POST /topups/{nonce} is open to anyone, and the nonce is public once the victim's AuthorizationUsed log is mined. The deposit watcher records the victim's refused transfer as UNATTRIBUTED with 'quote refused'. reexamine() never credits such rows automatically (`if detail.startswith(SEVERAL_SENDERS) or QUOTE_REFUSED in detail: # Never credited automatically`), even after the victim links the paying wallet.
kept.failure_scenario: 1) A victim mints a $100 quote with nonce N and pays T1 (100 USDC, block b). 2) An attacker reads N from the AuthorizationUsed topic of T1 and sends its own transferWithAuthorization(from=attacker, to=pay_to, value=10, nonce=N) as T2 in block b+1. 3) The attacker POSTs /topups/N with T2 before the victim's client redeems or the watcher's next 60 s scan. The quote becomes CREDITED with $0.00001. 4) The victim's T1 is refused with 409 topup_already_credited. The watcher marks it unattributed / quote refused for good, and the victim's balance is $0.00001 for $100 paid. Recovery needs a manual operator credit. Variant: if the victim's signed authorization leaks before mining (relayer or facilitator), the attacker can bundle [dust auth over N, victim auth over N] in one transaction. verify_transfer then takes the first bound payment and credits the dust, and the 100 USDC row is recorded CREDITED (final).

kept.prod_reachability: Any hub with AIMARKET_TOPUP_ENABLED=1 (quotes). Worse with AIMARKET_DEPOSIT_WATCH on (default 1 when AIMARKET_TOPUP_PAY_TO is set), because the well-known tells payers that presenting is optional, which leaves the attacker a window of up to the 60 s interval. The official scripts/credits_topup_pay.py presents promptly but sleeps 6 s between retries after a 409.

Credit each distinct authorization over the nonce up to the quote total (key spent payments on nonce+authorizer, and keep the quote open until paid_units >= amount_units), or bind a quote to the first payer wallet. At minimum, have the watcher credit a refused transfer whose reason is topup_already_credited to the quote's own account under its own chain:<tx> reference.

kept.title: Transient JSON-RPC errors are classified as 'payment_invalid' and the deposit watcher never redeems the quote payment again
kept.mechanism: topup.redeem decides retryability by matching text: `except settle.PaymentError as exc: text = str(exc); pending = "confirmation" in text or "not on chain yet" in text; raise TopupError(409 if pending else 402, ..., retryable=pending)`. settle._rpc raises PaymentError for any JSON-RPC error body (`if "error" in body: raise PaymentError(f"chain rpc refused {method}: ...")`). verify_transfer calls `head = int(_rpc(used, "eth_blockNumber", [], timeout), 16)` outside any try, and with a single settle URL it re-raises the transport PaymentError (wrong chain id, unparsable reply). A provider rate-limit returned as HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC error becomes a non-retryable 402. In the watcher, _redeem_quotes puts that in `refused`, records the row UNATTRIBUTED with 'quote refused', and reexamine() never retries the redemption. The transaction is re-read only if it falls inside the 12-block overlap of the next scan, which happens 30 blocks later.
kept.failure_scenario: A buyer pays a $20 quote and relies on the watcher. During the scan, the node that returned the receipt answers eth_blockNumber with {"error":{"code":-32005,"message":"rate limit"}}. The redemption is refused as payment_invalid, the deposit row becomes unattributed / quote refused, and the quote stays 'quoted'. Every later scan, with the node healthy again, leaves it unattributed. 20 USDC sits in the top-up wallet uncredited until the buyer re-presents by hand or the operator credits it.
kept.evidence: topup.py:592-596 (text-matched classification; PaymentFinal is never consulted); settle.py:341-342 (_rpc → PaymentError on a JSON-RPC error); settle.py:425-426 (single-URL transport error re-raised); settle.py:431 (eth_blockNumber outside try); deposit_watch.py:443-448 and 469-471 (non-retryable → refused → UNATTRIBUTED); deposit_watch.py:554-561 (never retried). git log: 96a32ec50 introduced PaymentFinal for exactly this distinction, but topup.redeem does not use it.
kept.prod_reachability: Hubs with AIMARKET_TOPUP_ENABLED=1 and the deposit watcher on (AIMARKET_TOPUP_PAY_TO set, AIMARKET_DEPOSIT_WATCH default 1). Public Base RPCs are the default settle list. The single-URL branch applies when AIMARKET_SETTLE_RPC_URL names one node.
kept.repro_notes: Scratch test test_transient_jsonrpc_error_strands_quote_payment_as_refused (same file). settle._rpc raises PaymentError('chain rpc refused eth_blockNumber: ... rate limit') once. After that scan the row is UNATTRIBUTED with QUOTE_REFUSED. Three more scans with a healthy node leave it unattributed, the quote is still 'quoted' and the balance is 0.
kept.suggested_fix: In topup.redeem, treat only settle.PaymentFinal as a final refusal (402 payment_invalid). Map every other PaymentError to 409/503 with retryable=True so the watcher keeps the row pending. Optionally let reexamine retry redemptions refused with payment_invalid that did not come from PaymentFinal.

verify.reasoning: settle._rpc raises PaymentError on any JSON-RPC error body (settle.py:331-341). verify_transfer's eth_blockNumber call (line 431) is outside the per-URL try, and with a single URL a receipt-lookup error is re-raised (425-426). topup.redeem (592-596) classifies by text match ('confirmation' / 'not on chain yet') and never checks settle.PaymentFinal, so a transient provider error becomes a non-retryable 402 payment_invalid. The watcher puts it in `refused`, which ends as UNATTRIBUTED with QUOTE_REFUSED (deposit_watch.py:443-471). reexamine never retries such rows (554-561), and a 12-block overlap does not re-read it. The trigger depends on a provider answering HTTP 200 with a JSON-RPC error (rate limit or similar) rather than HTTP 429; a 429 goes through raise_for_status, then `except Exception`, then 503 retryable, which is safe. The quote stays 'quoted', so the buyer or operator can re-present it by hand, but the automatic path is dead.

kept.title: Deposit watcher can permanently skip deposits when eth_getLogs is answered by a node lagging behind the one that gave the head
kept.mechanism: scan_once takes `head` from one eth_blockNumber call and reads eth_getLogs windows up to `safe = head - (min_conf-1)`. It then advances the cursor (`self.store.set_cursor(key, end + 1)`) whatever the log node actually had (`logs = self.rpc("eth_getLogs", ...) or []`). Watcher.rpc goes through settle.rpc_call → chain_net.pool_for_urls(rotate=True), so successive calls are spread over up to 5 heterogeneous public Base providers. A node that clamps a range extending beyond its own head returns a short or empty result without error. The next scan re-reads only OVERLAP_BLOCKS=12 behind the cursor. A transfer in a block more than about 13 blocks (26 s) ahead of the log node's head is never seen. No row is written (not even unattributed), and no balance reconciliation exists.
kept.failure_scenario: A linked wallet sends 5 USDC at block 980. eth_blockNumber (node A) answers 1000, so safe=999. eth_getLogs for ..999 goes to node B whose head is 974 and returns []. The cursor is set to 1000. Later scans read from 988 onward. The 5 USDC is never credited, never listed in /admin/deposits, never counted for the alerter. A quote payment missed this way can still be presented by hand; a plain transfer from a linked wallet is lost silently.
kept.evidence: deposit_watch.py:606 `head = int(self.rpc("eth_blockNumber", []), 16)`; :615-617 eth_getLogs `or []`; :642 `self.store.set_cursor(key, end + 1)`; :65 `OVERLAP_BLOCKS = 12` (the comment assumes a backend is only 'a block or two behind'); :373 rpc via settle.rpc_call; chain_net.py:850-869 pool_for_urls rotate=True; chain_net.py:181-191 five public Base presets.

Whether loss happens depends on a provider silently clamping ranges past its head (older op-geth / some load-balanced gateways); providers that return an error are safe (Retry and re-read).

kept.suggested_fix: Pin one endpoint per scan for eth_blockNumber and eth_getLogs, or after each window confirm on the same URL that its head is at least `end` (or filter by blockHash). Cap `safe` by the lowest head seen. Add a periodic deep re-scan (for example the last 1800 blocks hourly) and a reconciliation of the wallet's on-chain balance against recorded deposits.

kept.title: With a market fee enabled, the invoke 402 names the seller as payTo, but verification requires payment through the splitter, so every x402 buyer pays and is refused
kept.mechanism: The 402 middleware builds the offer from request.state.x402_pay_to, which _bind_listing_payee sets to settle.seller_pay_to(cap) (the seller). It mints the invoice with pay_to=seller. settle.terms_for sets `offer_to = splitter` when AIMARKET_MARKET_FEE_BPS>0 and AIMARKET_MARKET_SPLITTER is set, and verify_transfer then requires the authorization's own transfer to go to the splitter, followed by the splitter's two legs (`moved[1] == want_offer and ...`). x402.verify_payment is called with pay_to=terms.pay_to (the seller), so an authorization addressed to the splitter is also refused ('payment is addressed to somebody else'). PaymentTerms.as_x402_accept (payTo=offer_to) is never used by the 402 path. docs/money-rails.md:149 says 'With a fee the 402 always names the splitter'.
kept.failure_scenario: The operator enables the fee as documented (FEE_BPS=100 plus a deployed splitter). A buyer takes the 402 (payTo = seller, amount = gross, nonce N) and pays exactly that. _settle_market_payment → verify_transfer raises PaymentFinal 'the authorization for this nonce did not pay this call'. The buyer has paid the full price to the seller, the nonce is used on chain, and no call is served. If the buyer instead signs to the splitter, verify_payment refuses it before the chain check. No x402 sale can succeed while the fee is on.

kept.title: A mandated subcontracting allowance is journaled as an ordinary hold, so A2A crash recovery releases it, hands the whole allowance back to the mandate counters and reports "nothing was charged" after children were paid
kept.mechanism: ChargeJournal (a2a_tasks.py:482) tags an allowance only when its own hold_allowance() is called. When the root call is mandated, the ledger chain is MandatedCredits(ChargeJournal(credits)). MandatedCredits.hold_allowance goes to _reserved_hold(per_call=False), and that function always calls `self._inner.hold(...)` (mandates.py:1641), so the journal records kind "hold" for the alw_ receipt. _a2a_recover (hub_routes/agents.py:164-188) treats only kind "allowance" as unknowable. For a "hold" that is still 'held' it calls ledger.release_hold(alw) and then hub_mandates.settle(alw, 0). That releases the allowance with keep=0, so the mandate counters get the FULL allowance back, including what captured children spent. The task is then moved to AUTH_REQUIRED with outcome "released" ("Nothing was charged"), which invites a re-run. The A2A recovery runs on a 60 s timer, ahead of sweep_stale_allowances (grant expiry + 300 s). That sweep would have settled the mandate to the amount actually spent, but by then it finds the credit hold already released and skips it, so settle_grant is never recorded either.

kept.title: A failed verdict on a credits, x402 or other advisory call is signed as status="refunded" while the buyer's money was captured
kept.mechanism: plan() marks a call paid only when an X-Payment-Channel header is present (verified_settlement.py:1224). A credits (X-API-Key) or x402 seller-direct buyer who opts into verify is therefore 'advisory': the price is captured immediately (credits capture_hold / on-chain), but verification still runs. _finalize then sets `status="refunded" if refunding else "settled"` regardless of `paid`, overwrites the pending `reason: "advisory"` with `verify_failed`, signs the envelope, and returns it as the 200 response's `verification`. The docs tell clients that 'A refund is HTTP 200 with verification.status="refunded"'. The same predicate drift (`_Local.vs_deferred` = plan.active and plan.paid, invoke.py:135) also skips ACEX accrual and makes the provenance receipt state price 0 / 'refunded' when a buyer sends both X-API-Key and a channel, although credits captured the money.

Only the nested rejection_receipt.refunded=false tells the truth. Client SDKs following the docs report a refund that never happened. Likewise an x402 buyer whose USDC already went to the seller is told "refunded".

kept.title: Verified calls on escrow channels can become final after the buyer's authorization has expired: the ledger captures, but nothing can collect it on chain
kept.mechanism: The minimum lifetime the hub demands of a verified call's DebitAuthorization is `appeal_window_s() + _COLLECTION_MARGIN_S` (2 h). It ignores two delays. (1) The first verdict itself has no deadline: AIMARKET_VERIFY_MAX_WAIT_S=0, and transport errors retry forever. (2) An appeal filed at the end of the window is heard for up to AIMARKET_APPEAL_MAX_WAIT_S=21600 s (6 h > 2 h margin) before the first verdict stands. When the pass becomes final, _settle_hold calls capture_hold without checking the authorization deadline. The escrow mirror then finds `row.expired(now)` and abandons it ('this debit can no longer be collected on chain'). The checkpoint path (idempotency._expire_escrow) instead releases the hold when the authorization expired; the verified path does not.
kept.failure_scenario: AIMARKET_APPEAL_WINDOW_S=3600 means a minimum authorization lifetime of 10800 s. The verdict passes; the buyer appeals at minute 59 with a $0.02 bond; the court is slow or unreachable, and after 21600 s the appeal is indeterminate and the pass stands. The ledger captures at about t=25200 s, but the signature died at 10800 s, so the mirror abandons it. The seller who passed is never paid; the ledger shows the buyer charged while the escrow still holds the funds. The same happens without appeals when a Metis outage outlasts 2 h. The buyer's bond on an escrow channel is also uncollectable (see the related finding), so the buyer risks nothing by appealing.

kept.title: An unresolved verification freezes the buyer's whole channel indefinitely; most verifier failures retry forever and log nothing
kept.mechanism: _post_verify classifies every non-200 status except 400/401/413 as 'transport': 3xx (follow_redirects=False), 403, 404, 405, 422, 5xx, plus a RouteUnavailable route. With the default AIMARKET_VERIFY_MAX_WAIT_S=0, _run_claimed (scheduling.py:383-393) retries these forever and emits no log line for transport failures. While the row is 'pending'/'verifying' the channel hold stays 'held'. close() refuses any channel with a held hold (opening.py:705-716), the expiry sweep skips it (sweeps.py:76), and the reaper skips owned holds. There is no admin path to force-resolve a verified_settlements row. The docs present this as buyer-safe ('never captures buyer funds'), but the buyer cannot withdraw any of the channel balance, not just the held price.
kept.failure_scenario: An operator sets AIMARKET_VERIFY_METIS_URL=http://metis.example (nginx answers 301 to https), or Metis sits behind a proxy returning 502/403. Every verified invoke stays 'verifying' forever without a single log line. Each affected buyer's channel (say a $50 deposit with one $0.40 verified call) can never be closed or expire, so the full $50 is frozen until an operator notices and restarts with AIMARKET_VERIFY_MAX_WAIT_S>0 or fixes the URL. Oldest-first reaper scans (LIMIT 500) can also starve behind such owned holds.
kept.evidence: verifying.py:68-73 `if resp.status_code in (400, 401, 413): return "fatal"` / `if resp.status_code != 200: return "transport", f"http_{resp.status_code}"`; scheduling.py:385-389 `deadline = vs.max_wait_s()`, `if deadline > 0 and ...` (default 0); opening.py:705 'channel has N pending verified settlement(s) — retry close after they resolve'.
kept.prod_reachability: Default config (AIMARKET_VERIFY_MAX_WAIT_S unset); triggered by any persistent non-400/401/413 answer from the configured verifier or an unusable route key env.
kept.repro_notes: Traced by reading. The existing suite already shows that transport errors retry until a verdict; the close refusal is in channel_ledger/opening.py.
kept.suggested_fix: Log each transport failure (rate-limited) with the status. Treat 3xx/403/404/405/422 as fatal (configuration), not transient. Default AIMARKET_VERIFY_MAX_WAIT_S to a finite value (e.g. 24 h) after which policy applies. Optionally let close() release the buyer's free balance while leaving held cents in place.

kept.title: A refunded call that a later call's running-total authorization already superseded blocks collection of the whole escrow window
kept.mechanism: An escrow window carries one cumulative authorization. When call B arrives while row A at the same nonce is still PENDING, `verify_and_store` makes B sign A+B and abandons A with SUPERSEDED_REASON (authorization.py:208-212, 307-320). If A is then not charged, `withdraw(A)` is supposed to take it out of the window. Cases: a Pay-on-Verified fail verdict (finalizing.py:277-286 → _withdraw_escrow_authorization), or a slow concurrent call whose provider failed (local_delivery.py:809). But withdraw returns immediately because A is no longer PENDING/PLANNED (`if row is None or row.status not in (store.PENDING, store.PLANNED): return`). Row B keeps claiming A+B. Mirror guard 2 sums the ledger over the window (B's debit plus 0 for the released A), finds amount_units > allowed, and blocks with 'refusing to over-collect' on every pass until the deadline, then the row is abandoned. Later calls in the window inherit the inflated total.
kept.failure_scenario: A buyer on an escrow channel calls capability X with verify.requested (async verdict, $0.10). Row A is PENDING and its ledger hold is held. Seconds later the buyer calls Y ($0.05) and signs the $0.15 running total, which supersedes A. The Metis verdict for X fails, so its hold is released and withdraw(A) is a no-op. Row B ($0.15, ledger shows $0.05) is refused by guard 2 until its deadline and is then abandoned. Y and any further calls in that window (up to AIMARKET_ESCROW_MAX_UNCOLLECTED_USD=$5, after which the channel refuses new calls) are delivered but never collected. The same happens with two concurrent plain calls when the earlier one fails after the later one is stored.

"refusing to over-collect"`. This code is identical in the deployed 3.17.0 artifact.

Better: refuse to supersede a live row whose ledger hold is still unresolved (pending verdict or in-flight call), so the later call waits or opens the next window only after resolution.

kept.mechanism: When a market fee is on, terms_for sets offer_to = splitter (settle.py:227) and as_x402_accept advertises payTo = splitter with plain USDC EIP-712 extra (settle.py:161-180). Nothing tells the client it must call splitter.payWithAuthorization with a ReceiveWithAuthorization signature. A stock x402 client or facilitator signs TransferWithAuthorization(to=payTo) and calls USDC.transferWithAuthorization directly. USDC lands in the splitter without _settle running. The splitter has no owner, sweep or rescue, and pay()/payWithAuthorization pay only the measured delta of their own call (lines 141-143, 170-176). The stray balance can therefore never leave. The hub also rejects the payment: verify_transfer needs the splitter's two legs at index+2/+3, and the market route's x402.verify_payment compares authorization.to with the seller (hub_routes/payments.py:148, pay_to=terms.pay_to), so to=splitter fails as 'addressed to somebody else'.

The buyer is charged and not served, and the 1 USDC is unrecoverable by anyone. A buyer who follows the hub's own error text ('pay USDC on-chain to the seller payout_address') pays the seller the gross and is still refused for the missing fee leg.

The contract has no rescue function. settle.py:227 'offer_to = splitter' and settle.py:168 '"payTo": self.offer_to'. The settle.py:149-151 comment claims 'so an off-the-shelf x402 client can produce both legs with one signature', which is false: only first-party clients (pipeline_payments.py:17, hephaestus paidApi.ts:147) know to sign ReceiveWithAuthorization and call payWithAuthorization (selector 0x6e92be7a).

If that settle fails, or the process dies between the two writes, the mandate_holds row for alw_… stays 'held' with the full allowance amount. Neither sweep picks it up. sweep_stale_allowances only selects grants whose credit hold is still held (subcontract.py:403-404 `JOIN credit_holds h … WHERE h.status = 'held'`). The credit release of the allowance succeeds, but store.settle raises once (for example a lock or connection error on a busy hub). After any number of sweeps the mandate keeps counting $0.005 instead of $0.001 against perDay and, permanently, against `total`. For an agent near its total budget that means early mandate_limit refusals. Only issuing a new mandate gets around it. No funds are lost.

kept.title: HISTOR Watch on Postgres: concurrent settlement of two payments (or settle plus refund) for one subscription loses a period
kept.mechanism: settle() reads active_until with a plain SELECT, computes the new end in Python, and writes it back with UPDATE ... SET active_until=?. On SQLite, BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus a process lock serializes the transactions. On Postgres (READ COMMITTED, no SELECT ... FOR UPDATE), two transactions settling different payments of the same subscription both read E, and both write E+30d. _take_back has the same read-modify-write pattern. The per-payment conditional UPDATE prevents double-crediting one payment, but not lost updates on the subscription row.
kept.failure_scenario: A team has two open checkouts: renew hands out a second one when the first has less than 10 minutes left. It pays both, and the two checkout.session.completed webhooks (or a webhook plus the sweep or refresh) settle at the same moment on a Postgres-backed HISTOR. active_until ends at E+30d instead of E+60d, so one $29 payment buys nothing. A settle racing a refund can also ignore the refund.
kept.evidence: watch_paid.py:470-477 `sub = _subscription(tx, payment["subscription_id"])\n        current = _parse(sub["active_until"]) ... until = current + timedelta(days=int(payment["days"]))\n        tx.execute("UPDATE watch_subscriptions SET status='active', active_until=?, ..."`. db.py PostgresBackend.transaction is a plain `conn.transaction()` with no row lock.
kept.prod_reachability: Only with HISTOR_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://... (the commit 36e226bd8 says Watch was tested on Postgres) and Watch sales open. Needs two settlements for the same subscription at the same instant.
kept.repro_notes: Not executed: no Postgres in the sandbox. Traced by reading the transaction code.
kept.suggested_fix: Lock the subscription row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or tx.lock_log-style advisory lock keyed by subscription), or compute the end in SQL in one statement.

verify.reasoning: histor/histor/db.py PostgresBackend.transaction (lines 174-178) is a plain conn.transaction() at READ COMMITTED with no row lock. settle() (watch_paid.py:470-477) reads active_until with a plain SELECT, computes the new end in Python and writes an absolute value. Two concurrent settles of different payments for the same subscription can therefore lose one period, because the second UPDATE re-applies its own stale absolute value after the first commits. _take_back follows the same read-modify-write pattern. The SQLite backend serializes with BEGIN IMMEDIATE plus a process lock. Reaching this needs a Postgres deployment and two settlements, or a settle and a refund, of one subscription at the same instant. renew issues a second checkout only near the first one's expiry, so the race is unlikely. kept.title: Desk USDC settlement scan has no persisted cursor: transfers made while the scanner was down for more than about 73 min are never settled unattended
kept.mechanism: scan_payments always scans [head - confirmations - LOOKBACK_BLOCKS, head - confirmations] with LOOKBACK_BLOCKS = 2200 (about 73 min on Base) and keeps no last-scanned block. If the desk API is down, the RPC failover set is unavailable, or the scheduler is stopped for longer than that, transfers landing in the gap fall outside every later window. The invoice stays claimable for 24 h only through the buyer manually pasting a tx hash. Emberline's basepay.scan_payments (646-653) uses the same window.
kept.failure_scenario: A buyer gets an invoice, pays 49.014003 USDC, and closes the tab. The desk container is down for 2 h for maintenance or a host reboot. On restart the scan looks back only about 73 min, so the payment is never matched. The invoice expires and the key is never minted unless the buyer returns and pastes the hash within the 24 h grace window.

kept.repro_notes: Read-only trace.
kept.suggested_fix: Persist the last fully scanned block. On each tick scan from min(persisted+1, head-LOOKBACK) up to the head, covering at least the grace window (in chunks), and advance the cursor only after the walk completes.

kept.title: Spec and SDK docs promise that channel close settles or refunds, but the hub's close only updates its own ledger
kept.mechanism: Spec §6.1 says POST /channel/close is an 'HTTP request that asks the hub to submit settleChannel'. The Dart and TypeScript SDKs describe close as 'get a refund for the unused balance'. The hub's close() only flips the ledger row to 'settled'. For a transfer-funded channel it records an IOU (refund_executed_usd 0.0, refund_owed_usd = remainder). For an escrow-funded channel nothing is submitted on-chain: the depositor must call requestClose, wait SETTLE_WINDOW (1 h) and call settleChannel, or wait for expiry, to recover funds. The hub's sweep `--collect` expires only channels with used_units > 0.
kept.failure_scenario: A client built against the spec or SDK closes an escrow-backed channel and expects the remainder back. The on-chain channel stays Open with the buyer's balance until the buyer acts on-chain. On the custodial path the SDK surfaces `refund_usd` (an obligation) as if it were a refund. No funds are lost, but the buyer's balance stays locked until they act, and the claimed behavior is not implemented.
kept.evidence: spec.md:683 '| close | depositor | `POST /ai-market/v2/channel/close` ... | HTTP request that asks the hub to submit `settleChannel`. ...'; channel_ledger/opening.py:648-649 'Settlement is bookkeeping only: `refund_executed_usd` is always 0.0 here'; hub_routes/channels.py:122-142, where close_channel makes no chain call; aimarket-sdks/dart/lib/src/agent.dart:708 'Close a payment channel and get a refund for the unused balance.'
kept.prod_reachability: Every hub with AIFACTORY_CRYPTO_ENABLED=1, through the documented /channel/close API.
kept.suggested_fix: Correct spec §6.1 and the SDK docs: the close is ledger-only, the escrow remainder is reclaimed by the depositor via requestClose/settleChannel, and the transfer-path remainder is an operator obligation. Optionally have the SDK surface refund_status/refund_owed_usd.
